description: Operational view for the alula-liquidator keeper. Top row answers 'is the bot alive?'; middle rows answer 'what did it do and why?'; bottom rows answer 'is the plumbing healthy?'.

panels.title: Is the bot alive? (and doing anything)
Scrape up
panels.description: up{job="alula-keeper"}. 1 = Prometheus is reaching /metrics; 0 = the keeper is unreachable. Distinguishes 'bot dead' from 'bot up but idle'.

panels.title: Time since last successful scan
panels.description: time() - liquidator_last_successful_scan_timestamp_seconds. Green ≤30s, yellow ≤60s, red beyond. One value per market. Shows 'No data' before the first successful scan — pair with the Scrape up panel to disambiguate.

panels.title: Plans dispatched (1h)
panels.description: increase(liquidator_liquidation_plans_dispatched_total[1h]). Global counter (no market label). `or vector(0)` keeps the panel showing 0 (red) on fresh deploys instead of 'No data'.

panels.title: TXs confirmed (1h)
panels.description: increase(keeper_tx_confirmed_total{outcome="confirmed"}[1h]). Global counter (no market label). The bot is doing real work iff this is non-zero. `or vector(0)` shows red 0 on fresh deploy instead of 'No data'.

panels.title: XLM funding
panels.description: Keeper's XLM wallet balance (in XLM, not stroops). XLM funds inclusion fees; once it falls below `xlm_safety_margin` the bot stops submitting. Set the `xlm` dashboard variable to the XLM SAC contract address on your deployed network.

panels.title: Is the bot doing the right thing? — pipeline
Liquidation pipeline — plans → submitted → confirmed
panels.description: Steady-state: all three series track each other. Plans > submitted = simulation rejects in the executor path. Submitted > confirmed could be pending confirmations, poll failures, or finalization failures — check the TX confirmation outcomes panel for the cause.

panels.title: Scan loop — completed by outcome
panels.description: rate(liquidator_scan_completed_total[5m]) by outcome. 'ok' should dominate; 'no_obligations' is expected on quiet markets; 'no_market_data' on sustained basis means the data feed is broken.

panels.title: Obligations vs liquidatable positions
panels.description: Watched borrower count (liquidator_obligations_total) vs the subset currently flagged liquidatable per market. Sustained zero liquidatable with non-zero obligations is suspicious — likely engine/oracle drift.

panels.title: Skip reasons
panels.description: Why try_liquidate returned None. Fixed taxonomy of ≤8 reasons. A reason spiking 10× vs baseline is the early signal worth investigating.

panels.title: Simulation outcomes
panels.description: sum by (call, outcome) (rate(keeper_simulation_total[5m])). A growing 'not_liquidatable' bucket means engine/contract drift; growing 'error' means RPC trouble.

panels.title: TX submission outcomes
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(keeper_tx_submitted_total[5m])). 'retry_exhausted' or 'sim_empty' sustained is a red flag.

panels.title: TX confirmation outcomes
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(keeper_tx_confirmed_total[5m])). 'failed_on_chain' is the realisation-tax tail — tx made it to the network but ended FAILED (gas spent, nothing seized). 'submission_timeout' is uncertainty (tx may yet land). 'transport_error' / 'hash_decode_failed' indicate an RPC-layer regression.

panels.title: Wallet balances per asset
panels.description: Raw on-chain balances per asset the keeper holds. Falling to zero blocks Own/PreSwap liquidation modes and dust-stops the rebalancer. XLM caps inclusion-fee headroom (xlm_safety_margin).

panels.title: Keeper self-position per market
panels.description: The keeper's own jTokens (supply), dTokens (borrow), and plain collateral per market. The withdrawer strategy acts on the jToken series; non-zero dTokens mean the keeper is itself a borrower and is exposed to liquidation risk.

panels.title: XLM balance vs safety margin
panels.description: Live XLM balance overlaid against the configured xlm_safety_margin. The margin is the floor the rebalancer/liquidator refuse to spend below to preserve inclusion-fee headroom. When the balance line approaches the margin line, refill before the keeper starts skipping opportunities.

panels.title: Reactor back-pressure (dropped events)
panels.description: Any non-zero rate means the engine is dropping events because a downstream consumer (strategy, executor) couldn't keep up. Always operationally urgent.

panels.title: State persistence & sequence retries
panels.description: Cursor save failures = the keeper can't persist its event cursor (SQLite IO trouble). Bad-seq retries = stellar sequence-number contention on the signing key.

panels.title: Market scan latency (per-market quantiles)
panels.description: Wall-clock time spent inside one market evaluation, by outcome. Sustained p95 above ~1s usually means RPC roundtrips are slow (`read_market_data` or `read_user_obligation`); flat-but-rising p50 means more obligations are being checked. The `outcome` dimension separates fast early-exits (`no_market_data`, `no_obligations`) from full scans (`ok`).

panels.title: RPC simulate latency — p95 by contract function
panels.description: Per-function p95 of `simulate_transaction_envelope` roundtrips. This is the next-level-down view when `Market scan latency` looks bad — it tells you which contract call is slow (e.g. `get_market_data` vs `get_user_obligation` vs swap-provider quotes). Outcomes split `ok` from `transport_error` so failed RPCs don't dilute the latency signal.

panels.title: RPC simulate failures by function (rate/min)
panels.description: Per-function rate of failed simulate calls, split by `kind`: `transport` = network-layer error (RPC unreachable / 5xx), `sim_error` = the simulator returned a structured error response. Transport errors mean switch providers; sim_errors usually mean a contract input went bad.

panels.title: Expected profit per plan — p50 / p95 (USD)
panels.description: Per-market distribution of the expected net profit on each dispatched liquidation plan. Sourced from `plan.net_profit_oracle` at the moment the best (borrow, deposit) pair is picked, before tx submission — so this is the modelled gain, not realised. Oracle units divided by 10^7 (standard SAC scaling). p50 climbing means richer opportunities; p50 collapsing means we're scraping dust and should re-tune `min_profit_margin_cents`.

panels.title: Expected vs realised profit dispatched (USD/hour)
panels.description: Hourly run-rate of profit on dispatched plans, summed across markets. `expected total` counts the moment the liquidator decides to submit; `realised total` counts only when the resulting tx is confirmed on-chain. The gap between the two lines is the realisation tax (submission failures, simulation drift, retries exhausted). Both series are still modelled-not-on-chain-read — they use `plan.net_profit_oracle`, not the actual seized amount. Per-market `expected` series are included for breakdown.

panels.title: Rebalancer outcomes (per/min)
panels.description: What the rebalancer decided each time it ran or evaluated a candidate. `dispatched` is the only success outcome; everything else means it consciously did nothing. `nothing_to_swap` is normal (most assets already in target); `precondition_no_target` / `precondition_no_providers` means a config mistake; `evaluation_error` and `reservation_lost` mean trouble. A rebalancer silent in metrics is a rebalancer that isn't running — check the soroban-event topic filter or the `refresh_interval_blocks` cadence.

panels.title: Rebalancer dispatched swap size (USD p50 / p95)
panels.description: USD value distribution of swaps actually emitted. Sourced from `compute_value_cents(amount_in, info)` at dispatch time and divided by 100. The floor is `rebalancer_min_swap_amount_value_cents` from config; p50 hugging the floor means the rebalancer is bottom-feeding dust and you could relax (or tighten) the threshold to taste.

panels.title: Withdrawer outcomes (per/min)
panels.description: What the withdrawer decided on each deposit position it considered. `dispatched` = action emitted. `pool_at_capacity` / `below_threshold` are normal pauses (utilization safety floor or `min_withdraw_value_cents`). `no_obligations` is the steady state when the keeper isn't depositor on a market. `pool_missing` / `build_error` / `no_market_data` are red flags.

panels.title: Bad-debt initiator outcomes (per/min)
panels.description: Per-Liquidate-event decisions of the bad-debt request initiator. `ineligible` is the overwhelming common case (most liquidations leave healthy residual collateral). `dispatched` fires when a borrower is left underwater — i.e., the protocol needs to socialize the loss. `parse_error` / `decode_op_error` / `build_failed` indicate the strategy can't even evaluate eligibility — chase those in logs. Non-Liquidate event types are filtered upstream and don't count here.
